Task: Managed Metrics Monitoring

Write code that retrieves aggregated statistics for a metric over a time window using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Datadog:
  Service: Datadog Metrics API
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: submit_metrics, query_timeseries_points
  Setup hints: DD_API_KEY, DD_APP_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.datadoghq.com/metrics/custom_metrics/, https://docs.datadoghq.com/api/latest/metrics/

  Service: Azure Monitor Metrics
  SDK: azure-monitor-query
  Interface: sdk

  Setup hints: AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET

  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: get_metric_data, get_metric_statistics, list_metrics
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION

  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2513241.html, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/2513233.html

  Service: IBM Cloud Monitoring
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: POST /data, metric filters, aggregation expressions
  Setup hints: IBM_CLOUD_API_KEY, IBM_MONITORING_INSTANCE_ID, IBM_MONITORING_ENDPOINT
  Official docs: https://www.ibm.com/products/cloud-monitoring

Option 6 — Google Cloud Monitoring:
  Service: Cloud Monitoring
  SDK: google-cloud-monitoring
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: list_time_series, list_metric_descriptors
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/ref_v3/rest/v3/projects.timeSeries/list, https://cloud.google.com/monitoring/api/ref_v3/rest/v3/projects.metricDescriptors/list

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

```python
from google.cloud import monitoring_v3
from google.api import metric_pb2 as ga_metric
from google.api import monitor_pb2 as ga_monitor
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import os

def get_metric_statistics(
    project_id: str,
    metric_type: str,
    start_time: datetime,
    end_time: datetime,
    aggregation: str = "MEAN",
    alignment_period_seconds: int = 60
) -> list:
    """
    Retrieves aggregated statistics for a Google Cloud Monitoring metric over a time window.

    Args:
        project_id: Google Cloud project ID.
        metric_type: The metric type, e.g., "compute.googleapis.com/instance/cpu/utilization".
        start_time: Start of the time window.
        end_time: End of the time window.
        aggregation: The aggregation function (MEAN, SUM, COUNT, etc.).
        alignment_period_seconds: The alignment period in seconds for the time series.

    Returns:
        List of time series data points with aggregated values.
    """
    client = monitoring_v3.MetricServiceClient()
    project_name = f"projects/{project_id}"

    # Set up the time interval
    interval = ga_monitor.TimeInterval()
    interval.end_time.seconds = int(end_time.timestamp())
    interval.end_time.nanos = 0
    interval.start_time.seconds = int(start_time.timestamp())
    interval.start_time.nanos = 0

    # Set up the aggregation
    aggregation_obj = ga_monitor.Aggregation()
    aggregation_obj.alignment_period.seconds = alignment_period_seconds

    if aggregation == "MEAN":
        aggregation_obj.per_series_aligner = ga_monitor.Aggregation.Aligner.ALIGN_MEAN
    elif aggregation == "SUM":
        aggregation_obj.per_series_aligner = ga_monitor.Aggregation.Aligner.ALIGN_SUM
    elif aggregation == "COUNT":
        aggregation_obj.per_series_aligner = ga_monitor.Aggregation.Aligner.ALIGN_COUNT
    elif aggregation == "MAX":
        aggregation_obj.per_series_aligner = ga_monitor.Aggregation.Aligner.ALIGN_MAX
    elif aggregation == "MIN":
        aggregation_obj.per_series_aligner = ga_monitor.Aggregation.Aligner.ALIGN_MIN
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported aggregation: {aggregation}")

    aggregation_obj.cross_series_reducer = ga_monitor.Aggregation.Reducer.REDUCE_NONE

    # Build the query
    query = ga_monitor.ListTimeSeriesRequest(
        name=project_name,
        filter=f'metric.type="{metric_type}"',
        interval=interval,
        aggregation=aggregation_obj,
        view=ga_monitor.ListTimeSeriesRequest.TimeSeriesView.FULL
    )

    # Execute the query
    results = client.list_time_series(request=query)

    # Process the results
    time_series_data = []
    for series in results:
        for point in series.points:
            time_series_data.append({
                "timestamp": point.interval.end_time.ToDatetime(),
                "value": point.value.double_value if point.value.WhichOneof("value") == "double_value" else None
            })

    return time_series_data
```
